newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil swaps licences with BP.
newsitem.headline: Statoil swaps licences with BP.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had swapped interests in two Norwegian North Sea production licences with British Petroleum.
The deal gives Statoil and additional 2.5 percent in licence PL048 covering block 15/5 and brings its overall stake to 30.5 percent, or 60.5 percent with the government's direct financial interest.
Statoil recently acquired operatorship of the licence under a deal with Norsk Hydro ASA.
BP retains 8.4 percent of PL048 and acquires 10 percent of PL065, block 1/3, bringing its total stake in PL065 to 18.333 percent.
Statoil said the agreement on PL048 was in line with its goal to increase participation in projects it operates. Other partners in the licence are Norsk Hydro and operator Elf Aquitaine.
"This block contains an oil and gas discovery under eveluation for possible development," the company's Status Weekly newsletter said.
The deal on PL065 means Statoil has completely withdrawn from the acreage at the southern end of the Norwegian North Sea.
Other partners in PL065 are Enterprise Oil, Shell and the state's direct financial interest, which holds 30 percent.
